newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Sierra Leone coup to dominate Zimbabwe OAU meeting.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone coup to dominate Zimbabwe OAU meeting.

text.p: A coup in Sierra Leone is expected to dominate a two-day meeting of African foreign ministers starting in Zimbabwe on Thursday to prepare for an Organisation of African Unity summit.

The OAU has already condemned the Sunday military takeover, with OAU Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim saying it must be reversed because it undermined Africa's drive towards democracy and peaceful management of political problems.

Zimbabwean and OAU officials said there were indications that Sierra Leone's democratically-elected President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah who fled to neighbouring Guinea could come to the OAU summit next week to help keep pressure on his army rivals.
There has been overwhelming support for Kabbah at preparatory meetings for the June 2-4 OAU summit.

The Central Organ of the OAU Mechanism for Conflict Prevention, Management and Resolution appealed to the leaders of the Economic Community for West African States (ECOWAS) sub-region to ..."pursue efforts aimed at assisting the people of Sierra Leone in the restoration of constitutional order," a statement said.

"We call on all African and non-African countries not to take any action which would have the effect of giving comfort or strength to the leaders of the coup d'etat," they said, urging the international community to support these efforts.
Sierra Leone's U.N. ambassador James Jonah said on Tuesday Kabbah had asked regional states to restore his government and also demanded sanctions against the coup leaders.

The OAU's Salim is urging both the organisation's council of foreign ministers and the June 2-4 summit, which is expected to be attended by more than 40 leaders, including Laurent Kabila of the Democratic Republic of Congo, to take a tough stance against the coup leaders led by Major Johnny Paul Koromah.

Until Kabila's forces drove long-serving president Mobutu Sese Seko out earlier this month, OAU officials were expecting the conference in Zimbabwe's capital to be dominated by the fight for power in former Zaire, Africa's third largest country.
Salim said the OAU meetings would still discuss the Zaire situation, but now focusing on its transition programme to democracy.

The council of ministers will discuss the agenda of the summit, which will also focus on current peace efforts in Angola and Somalia, the war in Sudan, the establishment of an African Court of Human Rights, and Africa's economic problems and drive towards a common market.
The other big issue will be the election of an OAU secretary-general.
Salim, a former Tanzanian foreign minister and diplomat, who has headed the 53-member OAU since 1989, is seeking a third four-year term and is being challenged by Ivorian Foreign Minister Amara Essy.
